text.p: - The son of the Vladivostok's mayor has already spent 2-1/2 years in prison because his father refused to cooperate with local mafia, the paper says.

- Boris Pasternak's manuscripts, worth about 600,000 to 700,000 pounds sterling, will vanish into private collections if a Russian literary patron does not emerge to rescue Russia's rarity from an acution at Christie's in London.

- Although Russia's government is desperate to make the International Monetary Fund happy, the future of talks is uncertain, the paper says in reference to Russia's failure to meet IMF demands which would ensure the release of the latest tranche of an IMF loan.
- An unprecedented "terrorist" act at a Moscow cemetery on Sunday killed 13 people and wounded dozens of others.
- Elections to local administrations in unrecognised states which used to be part of the Soviet Union is a new step in gaining their independence.
- The bomb explosion which killed 13 people at a cemetery happening during the police's annual professional holiday has shown that police have no control over criminals in Russia.

- Boris Berezovsky, deputy secretary of the Security Council, will become the main peacemaker in Chechnya if an oil pipeline goes via the territory of the republic, Alexander Lebed says in an interview.
- By attacking the government's budget, parliamentarians are lobbying for the interests of various financial and industrial groups.
